absent: Coalesce get and set parameter handling beyond operation table advertisement and supported flag set
Ring sizing, channel count, link settings and flow classification callbacks referenced in operation table but without visible bodies
Device statistics retrieval transport and counter merge details beyond slot derivation and base zeroing
Transmit timeout, feature validation, interrupt moderation lifecycle, configuration change handling and physical port naming listed in lane header but outside visible range
Packet program dispatch beyond attachment validation and partial swap sequence, including transmit and redirect data paths
Page pool creation and destruction, affinity programming details, and control queue commands beyond guest offload programming
Receive polling, buffer replenishment, transmit completion and address mode work lifecycles
Queue reset transport specifics and reenable failure handling beyond status propagation

findings.text: The driver advertises an ethtool interface that groups steering, moderation, queue and link management. It declares support for frame count, microsecond delay and adaptive receive moderation, and provides handlers for receive steering table and key access with flow classification, for global and per queue moderation, for ring sizing and channel counts, for link state and settings with timestamp information, and for driver information, string tables, counters and receive ring count.

The driver exposes queue statistics operations with separate receive and transmit per queue handlers plus a base handler. Per queue handling initializes a collection context, gathers device reported values for a slot derived from queue position with receive on even positions and transmit on the following odd position, then merges driver maintained counters. The base handler reports stable starting values before aggregation across active queues.

Receive steering updates accept only preservation of the current hash function or selection of Toeplitz, rejecting other choices. Table replacement requires negotiated receive side scaling capability, while key replacement requires either scaling or hash reporting capability. The device is notified only when at least one of table or key was accepted, otherwise no command is issued.

Base queue statistics are defined as zero for packet and byte totals and for scheduling transitions, with extended drop, checksum, aggregation and rate limit fields present only when the corresponding device capability is advertised. Final values are produced by summing across the active receive and transmit queue ranges up to the configured maxima.

Device statistic capabilities are distinguished as separate groups named with a common prefix plus direction and category, covering transmit basic and receive basic, transmit checksum and receive checksum, transmit aggregation and receive aggregation, plus transmit speed and receive speed. Presence of each group controls whether matching base fields are initialized.

Suspend and resume form a paired lifecycle. Suspend drains configuration and address mode work, disables further mode work, closes the link when operational, then detaches the device. Resume rebuilds queues and page resources, marks the device ready, reenables mode work, reopens when previously operational, then attaches. Failure during resume resets the transport and releases any partially built queues and buffers.

Configuration changes during suspend and resume that open or close the link while operational are serialized by the global network configuration lock. Device detach and attach are serialized by the transmit lock with bottom halves disabled. Processor set stability during affinity programming is ensured by holding the CPU read lock.

Orphaned descriptors across all configured queue pairs are reclaimed in direction order, first transmit then receive, with voluntary scheduling cooperation between queues. Each detached buffer is handed to the direction specific release path so that transmit and receive resources are freed according to their own ownership rules.

Transmit completion can encounter socket buffers including orphaned variants, packet framework frames, or zero copy pool completions distinguished by a tag carried with the pointer. Each kind requires its own release action, and conflating them would corrupt memory accounting or stall zero copy completion.

Queue teardown guarantees that affinity state is cleared before transport queues are removed and that software queue memory is released last. Poll contexts for both directions are deleted first, then a network grace period elapses before the receive, transmit and control allocations are freed.

Queue bring up follows allocation then transport discovery then affinity programming, with full release of software queues if discovery fails. Affinity programming is performed only after successful discovery and under protection against processor set changes.

Transport queues are expected as repeating receive then transmit pairs with an optional trailing control queue. Receive and transmit completions use distinct callbacks, user visible names distinguish input and output instances with a separate control name, and receive context signalling is enabled for mergeable or small packet modes. Control presence also enables hardware virtual LAN filtering advertisement.

Minimum receive buffer size accounts for protocol headers plus the larger of device maximum transmission unit or architectural limit depending on packet mode, divided across ring capacity and rounded up. The result is clamped to at least header size and to a good packet floor after header removal.

Software queue allocation creates control state only when a control queue exists, plus paired transmit and receive arrays. Each pair receives polling contexts with distinct receive and transmit handlers and weights, initialized scatter tables, a packet length estimator, synchronized statistics, and a per receive queue moderation lock.

Guest offload programming converts a 64 bit mask to device byte order and issues a control message, reporting failure when the transport rejects it. Clearing and restoring are defined as no operation when no offloads are stored, otherwise they program zero or the stored mask respectively.

Guest offload control uses class VIRTIO_NET_CTRL_GUEST_OFFLOADS with operation VIRTIO_NET_CTRL_GUEST_OFFLOADS_SET to carry the feature mask. The mask itself is transported as a single 64 bit value in device byte order.

Receive zero copy binding attaches packet pool metadata and memory model only when a pool is supplied, then pauses reception, resets the transport queue with buffer unmapping, records the new pool, and resumes. Detach or reset failure results in a null pool with metadata unregistered, ensuring resume always occurs.

The generic queue reset operation provides disable with buffer recycling, optional completion notification, transport reset, then reenable as a single reusable primitive returning status. Callers supply recycling behavior and may omit completion handling.

Transmit zero copy binding pauses transmission, resets the transport queue using transmit specific recycling and completion, records the pool with failure forcing a null value, then resumes. Status of the reset is propagated to the caller.

Zero copy enable validates header room, presence of page resources to exclude large packet mode, queue range, and equality plus existence of receive and transmit DMA devices. Acquisition orders buffer storage, shared header mapping, pool DMA mapping, then receive followed by transmit binding, with any failure unwinding prior steps in reverse including unbinding, unmapping and freeing.

Mapping selects a bypass path when the queue does not use the mapping API, returning a physical address with sanitizer handling. Otherwise it rejects virtual allocations and delegates to page mapping, which prefers device specific operations when present and otherwise uses generic DMA with the queue DMA device.

Unmapping and error checking mirror mapping selection. Without the mapping API, unmap is a no operation and error checking reports success. With it, both delegate to device specific operations when present, otherwise to generic DMA using the same queue device.

Mapping must never operate on virtually remapped memory, and such attempts are rejected with a one time warning returning a mapping error. This guards DMA against addresses that lack stable physical backing.

Zero copy setup dispatches to enable when a pool is supplied and to disable otherwise. Disable validates queue range, unbinds receive and transmit while combining their status, then releases pool DMA, shared header mapping and buffer storage.

Packet program attachment is refused when maximum transmission unit exceeds page capacity minus headroom and shared metadata without fragment support, when mergeable buffers lack single page header support, and when the host provides receive offloads without a control channel to disable them. Excessive extra transmit queue demand does not refuse but proceeds in a slower locked mode with a warning.

Program swap takes an extra reference for the new program, pauses all reception and disables transmit polling when operational. Clearing removes per queue references, restores stored guest offloads once, and waits for network quiescence before resizing queues. Installing resizes first, then publishes references, clears offloads once when transitioning from absent, marks redirection support, with the reverse clearing that support on removal.
